Title: Diagnosis of test `testRoundTripNames` failure in `TarUtilsTest`

Details:
The test `testRoundTripNames` calls `checkName` method with multiple string inputs to assert that the string can be round-tripped through a byte array conversion and back without loss or modification.

- The `checkName` method creates a byte buffer of length 100.
- It then calls `TarUtils.formatNameBytes` to write the string bytes into this buffer.
- `formatNameBytes` copies character bytes from the input string to the buffer, up to the minimum of the string length or the buffer length, and pads the rest with zero bytes (NUL).
- The method returns `offset + length` as the length of written bytes, which appears to always be `offset + length` (in this case offset likely 0, length 100).
- Next, `checkName` calls `TarUtils.parseName` to convert the bytes back to a string.
- `parseName` reads bytes until it encounters a zero byte, stopping early and returning the accumulated characters so far.

This arrangement causes a fundamental inconsistency:
- `formatNameBytes` returns the full length of the buffer (100 bytes) even if the actual string is shorter and padded with zeros.
- `parseName` stops reading at the first zero byte, so trailing NUL bytes are ignored.
- The test expects a perfect round trip, so the input string and the result string must be equal.
- This will fail for strings that contain embedded zero bytes or whose returned length doesn't represent the actual data length but full buffer length.
- For example, the test commented out with `\0` (NUL) fails because the zero byte in the string causes premature truncation.
- Also, `formatNameBytes` returns `offset + length` which is misleading and causes the full buffer to be interpreted during parsing, although only part is actual data.

Hence, the bug lies in the mismatch between the length `formatNameBytes` returns and what `parseName` expects. `formatNameBytes` should return the actual length of the string data written (without including padding), and `parseName` should read exactly that many bytes to correctly reconstruct the string.

Suggested locations to fix:
- `org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarUtils.formatNameBytes(java.lang.String,byte[],int,int)`
- `org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarUtils.parseName(byte[],int,int)`

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
